Package neqsim.process.equipment.separator.emulsion

Class EmulsionSeparationStudy

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.separator.emulsion.EmulsionSeparationStudy
public final class EmulsionSeparationStudy extends Object
Runs an optional constant-area water-in-oil emulsion-layer diagnostic study.

The study owns its state and never changes a supplied separator, its outlets, or its transient inventory. It applies the dense-packed-zone model of Zlobin et al. (2026), DOI 10.1002/aic.70429. The supplied water rate is the dispersed-water rate entering the modeled layer, not necessarily the separator's total water rate. Effective horizontal interface area must be supplied explicitly. A horizontal drum requires a justified constant-area approximation.

Without calibrated kinetics, the default radius (1.35 mm) and contact-coalescence time (60 s) are disclosed screening guesses. The conversion omega = 1/(pi * radius^2 * contactTime) is an assumed effective contact area, not a published predictive chemistry law. Sensitivity scenarios are not confidence intervals or field validation.
